problem:
A tank has an inlet and an outlet. When the inlet is turned on, the rate at which water flows into the tank governed by the function

$$
r(t)=9{t}^{2}+18,
$$

where $r(t)$ is measured in liters per minute and $t>0$ is the time in minutes.

When the outlet is switched on, water leaves the tank through it at a rate of $14$ liters per minute.

The inlet is switched on, and the water level increases to $120$ liters, at which point the outlet is also switched on. How much water is in the tank $10$ minutes after switching on the outlet, given that the outlet is switched on at $t=0?$
worked_solution:
Water enters the tank at a rate of $9{t}^{2}+18$ liters per minute and leaves at a rate of $14$ liters per minute. Therefore, the **rate of change of volume** (call it $R(t)$) is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(t) & =r(t)-14 \\  & =9{t}^{2}+18-14 \\  & =9{t}^{2}+4\end{aligned}
$$

To find the **total volume** of water in the tank after $t$ minutes (call it $T(t)$), we apply the second fundamental theorem of calculus:

$$
\begin{aligned}T(t) & =T(0)+{\int }_{0}^{t}R(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =120+{\int }_{0}^{t}(9{x}^{2}+4)\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

To ensure that $T$ is a function of $t$ only, we use a different variable ($x$) for the integration. 

To find out the volume of water after $10$ minutes, we substitute $t=10$ into the above and evaluate.

$$
\begin{aligned}T(10) & =120+{\int }_{0}^{10}(9{x}^{2}+4)\,\text{d}x \\  & =120+{[3{x}^{3}+4x]|}_{0}^{10} \\  & =120+[(3(10)^{3}+4(10))-(0)] \\  & =120+3040 \\  & =3\,160\end{aligned}
$$
